section.heading: Purpose.
section.text: This regulation applies to all Political Subdivisions that receive funds from the Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund.

annotations.annotation: 53:17 26-094-E (Regulations .01 — .09) EMERGENCY ACTION IN EFFECT 7/20/2026 — 1/16/2027

para.text: In this subtitle, the following terms have the meanings indicated.
Terms Defined.
“Community-Based Organizations” means a nonprofit organization where community residents are involved in program design, implementation, and evaluation, often taking on leadership roles.
“Disproportionately Impacted Areas” has the meaning stated in Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, §36–101, Annotated Code of Maryland.
“Fund” has the meaning stated in Alcohol Beverages and Cannabis Article, §1-3A-01, Annotated Code of Maryland.
“Internal Controls” means processes, policies, and procedures implemented by a Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund commission to ensure effectiveness and efficiency of operations.
“Low-Income Communities” means a geographic area, or the residents of a geographic area, that is either:
Designated as a Qualified Census Tract by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development under 26 U.S.C. §42(d)(5)(B)(ii); or

For a Political Subdivision in which two or fewer census tracts are designated as Qualified Census Tracts, an area in which at least 51 percent of households earn at or below 80 percent of the area median income, as determined by the most recent data published by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development.

“Nonprofit” means a tax-exempt entity under the Internal Revenue Code of the United States, 26 U.S.C. §501(c), organized for charitable, educational, or socially beneficial purposes, that is qualified to do business and in good standing with the Maryland Department of Assessments and Taxation.
“Office” has the meaning stated in Alcohol Beverages and Cannabis Article, §1–3A–01, Annotated Code of Maryland.
“Political Subdivision” has the meaning stated in Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, §1-101, Annotated Code of Maryland.

“Public Hearing” means a hearing subject to the Open Meetings Act, General Provisions Article, §§3-301—3-501, Annotated Code of Maryland, held by a Political Subdivision for the express purpose of receiving public comment and ensuring public participation in the decision-making process.
Administrative Expenses.

Political Subdivisions may use up to 15 percent of the funds received from the Fund in the fiscal year for administrative expenses incurred by the Political Subdivision in managing or administering the funds.
In general, administrative expenses include the costs of overall program management, budgeting, monitoring, reporting, and evaluation. Eligible administrative expenses are limited to:
Salary expenses for employees related to managing the funds;
Technology related to administration of the funds;
Fees for professional services related to the administration of the funds;
Employee training related to the administration of the funds;
Consulting or legal services related to the administration of the funds;
Technology systems used for fund tracking or reporting related to the administration of the funds; and
Community and stakeholder engagement, and public hearing expenses related to the administration of the funds.

Political Subdivisions shall certify that administrative expenses are reasonable and proportionate to the overall funding disbursed and in compliance with statutory limits established by Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, §1-3A-03, Annotated Code of Maryland.
Financial Accountability and Fund Management. Money expended from the Fund must be:
Supplemental to, and may not supplant, funding that otherwise would be appropriated for preexisting programs; and
Held separately from other revenue and general funds.

section.heading: Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund Commissions.

para.text: Political Subdivisions may establish a commission to support or assume the decision-making authority of the Political Subdivision to utilize money expended from the Fund.

Commission Membership. A commission shall include at least five members who collectively possess the requisite expertise in community advocacy, social services, economic development, and fiscal oversight, including:
A resident of a Disproportionately Impacted Area;
An individual impacted by the criminal justice system;
An individual knowledgeable about the impacts of cannabis criminalization on communities;
An individual with experience in providing services for recently incarcerated individuals reentering the community;
An individual with expertise in small business development, job training, and adult professional development; and
An individual having demonstrated expertise or experience in accounting, business, financial management, budgeting, or related fiscal oversight functions.
Internal Controls. Commissions shall establish procedures for internal controls through a public engagement process.
Before utilizing any money expended from the Fund, a Political Subdivision shall develop a plan in consultation with stakeholders.
The plan must be the subject of a Public Hearing. The Public Hearing shall:
Include time for public questions and responses;
Be publicized at least 14 days in advance;
Be held at a time and location accessible to individuals living in Disproportionately Impacted Areas; and
Provide opportunity for written comment.

The plan shall be approved by the Political Subdivision’s governing body and submitted to the Office for reporting purposes. All Political Subdivisions shall submit a plan to the Office by October 1, 2026.
The plan must:
Include assessment data to rank community needs;
Reflect community input; and
Describe outreach efforts to Low-Income Communities.

section.heading: Allowable Uses and Expenditures Guidelines.
section.text: Allowable uses for funds received from the Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund are defined by Alcoholic Beverages and Cannabis Article, §1-3A-03(a)(6), Annotated Code of Maryland.

para.text: Reporting Requirements.
On or before October 1, 2026, and each October 1 thereafter, each Political Subdivision shall submit a report to the Office.
Reports shall be submitted in the format, manner, and on the schedule prescribed by the Office.
Reports shall include:
Total funds received;
Any funds carried over from the prior year or years;
Total funds utilized;
Name and email of Fund point of contact;
Name or names of any entity receiving awards;
Award amount or amounts
Description of the services or programs funded and population served;
Duration or term of the funding agreement; and
Administrative Expenses:
Salary expenses for employees related to managing the funds;
Fees for professional services related to the administration of the funds;
Employee training related to the administration of the funds;
Technology related to administration of the funds;
Community and stakeholder engagement, and public hearing expenses related to the administration of the funds; and
The methods used by the Political Subdivision to solicit, review, and select entities that may be eligible to receive funds; and
The Office may request information at any time related to the annual report.

section.heading: Audit Requirements.
section.text: The Office of Legislative Audits shall audit the Fund as provided under State Government Article, §2-1220, Annotated Code of Maryland.

section.heading: Non-Compliance Protocols.
section.text: The Office may recommend corrective measures in cases of non-compliance with fund distribution plans or the establishment of a Community Reinvestment and Repair Fund Commission.

para.text: Lawful Gear.
A person may catch or attempt to catch crabs in the tidal waters of Maryland only with the gear authorized in this chapter.

Diving Apparatus. A person may not possess, catch, or attempt to catch crabs in the tidal waters of Maryland using diving apparatus by itself, or in conjunction with any of the other methods authorized in this chapter.
Gear designated to catch or attempt to catch crabs and defined in this chapter, except for a seine, is not considered a net under the definition listed in COMAR 08.02.05.02.
Recreational Gear — Definitions.
The gear defined in this section may be used to catch or attempt to catch crabs for recreational purposes.
“Bushel” means a:
Circular container with the following inside dimensions:
18 inches top diameter;
13-1/2 inches bottom diameter; and
12 inches height; or
Rectangular container with the following inside dimensions:
11 inches height;
19½ inches length; and
12½ inches width.
“Collapsible crab trap” means a manually operated, portable device:
Having a flat bottom not more than 20 inches by 15 inches, and not more than four articulated sides; and
Designed so that failure to apply manually exerted tension on the closing mechanism allows the crabs to escape.
“Crab net ring” means a manually operated, portable device that:
Consists of:
Two rings, each of a different diameter, connected by netting, where the larger of the two rings shall be less than or equal to 30 inches in diameter; or
One ring that shall be less than or equal to 30 inches in diameter, connected to netting;
When baited and lowered to the bottom, lies flat on the bottom; and
When pulled to the surface, forms a deep pocket out of the netting.
“Crab pot” means a cube-shaped or rectangular shaped device with openings toward the inside for the entrance of crabs.
“Dip net” means a mesh bag of netting or wire which is suspended from a circular, oval, or a rectangular frame attached to a handle.
“Handline” means an unbuoyed fishing line managed primarily by hand.
“Trotline” means a length of rope or line, buoyed at both ends with one or more anchors, which is baited without hooks or snares at intervals for the purpose of catching crabs.
“Seine” means an encircling type of net which is not more than 50 feet long and 5 feet wide.
Commercial Gear.
In addition to the gear listed in §B(2)—(8) of this regulation, the gear defined in this section may also be used for commercial crab harvesting.
“Bank trap” means an enclosure constructed of wire mesh not more than 4 feet long and not more than 4 feet wide, with a single row of hedging not more than 75 feet long.
“Barrel” means a container which holds not more than 2-1/2 U.S. standard bushels of crabs and does not exceed the following inside dimensions:
20½ inches across the top diameter;
27½ inches height; and
18 inches along the bottom diameter.
“Channel pound” means an enclosure constructed of wire mesh not more than 8 feet long and not more than 4 feet wide, with two rows of hedging, each not longer than 100 feet long.
“Crab scrape” means a scoop or other device which is dragged along the bottom for the purpose of catching crabs.
“Hand scrape” means a single scoop or other device which is:
Dragged along the bottom for the purpose of catching crabs; and
Retrieved by hand without the aid of any mechanical device during any stage of the retrieval.
“Lug” means a rectangular-shaped container that does not exceed the following inside dimensions:
22-7/8 inches in length across the top;
14-7/8 inches in width across the top;
21 inches length across the bottom;
13 inches width across the bottom; and
12-3/8 inches height.

para.text: A person may not use patent tongs to catch or attempt to catch oysters in any of the waters listed in this section.
Tidal waters of the following counties, other than those waters included as part of the Chesapeake Bay, Tangier Sound, and Pocomoke Sound as defined by COMAR 08.02.01.06B:
Wicomico County;
Queen Anne’s County, except as provided in §B(5) of this regulation;
Talbot County;
Dorchester County; and
Kent County, except as provided in §§B(1)—(4) of this regulation.
Patuxent River, except as provided in §B(6) of this regulation.
Tributaries of the Potomac River.

The recreational season, daily catch limits, days of the week, and times for catching oysters shall be established, and may be modified, through a public notice issued in accordance with Regulation .11 of this chapter.
The Department shall issue a public notice that establishes the parameters described in §A of this regulation for the recreational oyster fishery not later than July 1 of each year.

Prohibition. Except as specified in this regulation and in any public notice issued in accordance with Regulation .11 of this chapter, it is illegal for a person to catch oysters for recreational purposes.
Lawful Methods. A person may catch or attempt to catch oysters for recreational purposes only by hand, rake, shaft tong, or diving with or without scuba equipment.
A person may not take oysters for recreational purposes while aboard a vessel where any other person is engaged in commercial oystering.
Season, Days, and Catch Limits.

The season for catching oysters and the days of the week that an individual may catch oysters for commercial purposes shall be established for each gear type, and may be modified, through a public notice issued in accordance with Regulation .11 of this chapter.
The daily commercial catch limits shall be established for each gear type, and may be modified, through a public notice issued in accordance with Regulation .11 of this chapter.
The Department shall issue a public notice that establishes the parameters described in §A(1) and (2) of this regulation for the commercial oyster fishery not later than July 1 of each year.

Lawful Methods. A person may catch or attempt to catch oysters for commercial purposes only by shaft tong, patent tong, diving apparatus, dredge boat, dredge boat propelled by means of an auxiliary yawl boat, or power dredge.
Times for Catching.
During an open season in November and December, a person may catch or attempt to catch oysters for commercial purposes only from:
Sunrise until sunset when using shaft tong, patent tong, diving apparatus, dredge boat, or dredge boat propelled by means of an auxiliary yawl boat; and
Sunrise until 3 p.m. when using a power dredge.
Except as described in §C(1) of this regulation, during an open season a person may catch or attempt to catch oysters for commercial purposes only from:
Sunrise until 3 p.m. when using shaft tong, patent tong, dredge boat, diving apparatus, or power dredge; and
Sunrise until sunset when using a dredge boat propelled by means of an auxiliary yawl boat.
An individual who harvests oysters for commercial purposes shall deliver oysters:
To a person who is licensed and certified to sell shellfish by the Maryland Department of Health in accordance with COMAR 10.15.04 and 10.15.07; and
Not later than 9 p.m. on the same day of harvest.
A person may not land or possess oysters on a vessel more than 2 hours after sunset or anytime before sunrise.
An individual shall notify the Natural Resources Police when there is an emergency which would prevent compliance with the times specified in §§C and D of this regulation.
Oysters may only be sold in accordance with COMAR 08.02.08.02.

In addition to the requirements of this chapter, a commercial licensee shall harvest oysters in accordance with the National Shellfish Sanitation Program Model Ordinance that is incorporated by reference by the Maryland Department of Health in COMAR 10.15.07.01A.

Notice shall be provided to the Department in advance of each day a dredge boat is propelled in accordance with §A of this regulation.
General.
Notwithstanding Natural Resources Article, §4-1012(b), Annotated Code of Maryland, a power dredge may only be used in the following areas:
Leased areas;

Power Dredge Study Areas established in §C of this regulation; and
Portions of the Wild Grounds Study Area established in §D(1) of this regulation that have been opened in accordance with §E of this regulation.
A person may not use or possess a power dredge bar that is more than 42 inches in length measuring from the outside teeth or that exceeds a weight of 200 pounds.

then running 67° True to a point defined by Lat. 38°42.825’ N, Long. 76°18.214’ W; then running 193° True to a point defined by Lat. 38°42.667’ N, Long. 76°18.262’ W; then running 86° True to a point on the shore west of Nelson Point defined by Lat. 38°42.767’ N, Long. 76°16.527’ W; then running southeasterly along the shore to a point on the shore at Nelson Point defined by Lat. 38°42.549’ N, Long. 76°16.281’ W; then running 61° True to a point on the south side of Bridge Creek, defined by Lat. 38°43.440’ N, Long. 76°14.196’ W; then running southerly along the shore to a point on the shore at Holland Point defined by Lat. 38°41.879’ N, Long. 76°13.611’ W; then running 186° True to a point defined by Lat. 38°41.838’ N, Long. 76°13.617’ W; then running 92° True to a point on the shore at Lucy Point defined by Lat. 38°41.825’ N, Long. 76°13.178’ W; then running southeasterly to a point on the shore of Ferry Neck, defined by Lat. 38°40.354’ N, Long. 76°12.083’ W; then running 144° True to a point on the shore at Benoni Point defined by Lat. 38°40.249’ N, Long. 76°11.969’ W; then running 96° True to a point on the shore at the north side of Boone Creek, defined by Lat. 38°40.090’ N, Long. 76°10.138’ W; then running 118° True to a point on the shore at the south side of Boone Creek, defined by Lat. 38°40.011’ N, Long. 76°9.954’ W; then running then running southeasterly along the shore to a point on the shore at the north side of Island Creek, defined by Lat. 38°39.697’ N, Long. 76°9.699’ W; then running 120° True to a point on the shore at the south side of Island Creek, defined by Lat. 38°39.517’ N, Long. 76°9.300’ W; then running southeasterly along the shore to the point of beginning.
Power Dredge Study Areas. An individual may catch or attempt to catch oysters only by power dredge in the areas listed in §C(1)—(3) of this regulation.
Queen Anne’s County Power Dredge Study Areas:

All of the waters of Eastern Bay enclosed by a line beginning at a point defined by Lat. 38°53.805’ N, Long. 76°15.450’ W; then running 274° True to a point defined by Lat. 38°53.831’ N, Long. 76°15.920’ W; then running 313° True to a point defined by Lat. 38° 54.060’ N, Long. 76° 16.230’ W; then running 53° True to a point defined by Lat. 38°54.482’ N, Long. 76°15.511’ W; then running 91° True to a point defined by Lat. 38°54.476’ N, Long. 76°15.059’ W; then running 199° True to a point defined by Lat. 38°54.130’ N, Long. 76°15.213’ W; then running 210° True to the point of beginning; and

All of the waters of Eastern Bay enclosed by a line beginning at a point defined by Lat. 38°52.672’ N, Long. 76°18.659’ W; then running 304° True to a point defined by Lat. 38°52.995’ N, Long. 76°19.265’ W; then running 36° True to a point defined by Lat. 38°53.465’ N, Long. 76°18.825’ W; then running 122° True to a point defined by Lat. 38°53.160’ N, Long. 76°18.211’ W; then running 216° True to the point of beginning.

Kent County Power Dredge Study Area. All of the waters of the Chesapeake Bay enclosed by a line beginning at a point defined by Lat. 39°7.690’ N, Long. 76°18.868’ W; then running 5° True to a point defined by Lat. 39°8.482’ N, Long. 76°18.772’ W; then running 111° True to a point defined by Lat. 39°8.258’ N, Long. 76°18.038’ W; then running 111° True to a point defined by Lat. 39°8.114’ N, Long. 76°17.546’ W; then running 170° True to a point defined by Lat. 39°7.603’ N, Long. 76°17.432’ W; then running 272° True to a point defined by Lat. 39°7.623’ N, Long. 76°18.167’ W; then running 277° True to the point of beginning.

Dorchester County Power Dredge Study Area. All of the waters of Holland Straits enclosed by a line beginning at a point defined by Lat. 38°6.359' N, Long. 76°3.752' W, then running 273° True to a point defined by Lat. 38°6.385' N, Long. 76°4.481' W, then running 2° True to a point defined by Lat. 38°6.840' N, Long. 76°4.463' W, then running 95° True to a point defined by Lat. 38°6.790' N, Long. 76°3.749' W, then running 180° True to the point of beginning.
Wild Grounds Study Area.

The study area consists of all of the waters of Eastern Bay enclosed by a line beginning at a point defined by Lat. 38°53.160' N, Long. 76°18.211' W; then running 302° True to a point defined by Lat. 38°53.465' N, Long. 76°18.825' W; then running 36° True to a point defined by Lat. 38°53.633' N, Long. 76°18.668' W; then running 124° True to a point defined by Lat. 38°53.320' N, Long. 76°18.063' W; then running 216° True to the point of beginning.
A commercial licensee may not harvest oysters with a power dredge in this area unless authorized by public notice in accordance with §E of this regulation.
Public Notice.
In order to evaluate the potential effects of power dredging, the Department may, by public notice:
Open or close portions of the areas defined in §§C(2) and D(1) of this regulation to the harvest of oysters; or
Specify gear that may be used in portions of the area defined in §D(1) of this regulation.
If it is determined necessary to maintain surface shell, the Department may by public notice establish the following:
Portions of the areas defined in §§C(2) and D(1) of this regulation in which maintenance is necessary;
Allowable gears for maintenance;
A requirement to receive prior written permission by the Department to perform maintenance on the area;
Number of licensees who may perform maintenance on the area; and
Dates and times during which the maintenance may be performed.
The public notice shall state its effective hour and date and shall be published on the Fisheries Service website at least 48 hours in advance of the effective hour and date.

The Secretary shall make a reasonable effort to disseminate a public notice issued under this section through various other media so that an affected individual has a reasonable opportunity to be informed.
A violation of the restrictions set by the Secretary in accordance with this section is a violation of this regulation.

section.heading: Black Bass — Largemouth Bass and Smallmouth Bass.

para.text: Size Limit. The minimum size for black bass is:
12 inches total length from June 16 through the end of February; and
15 inches total length from March 1 through June 15.
Catch Limit. An individual may not possess more than five black bass.
Gear Restrictions.
An individual may not catch or attempt to catch black bass in any manner in the tidal waters of the State except with rod or hook and line using natural or artificial baits.
An individual shall immediately return unharmed to the water any black bass caught in a net, seine, or other device while engaged in other fishing.
General Prohibitions. Except as provided in COMAR 08.02.14, an individual may not sell, offer to buy or sell, expose for sale, or purchase any black bass at any time.

section.heading: Use of Hard-Shell Clam Dredges in Tangier Sound and Pocomoke Sound.

para.text: Size of Dredge. A person may not catch or attempt to catch hard-shell clams in the waters of Tangier Sound and Pocomoke Sound with a hydraulic dredge or mechanical dredge more than 36 inches in width.

Areas Where Hard-Shell Clams May Be Taken by Dredge. Subject to Regulation .05 of this chapter and except as provided in §C of this regulation, an individual licensed to catch hard-shell clams may catch or attempt to catch hard-shell clams with a dredge only in the waters of:
Tangier Sound that are bounded on the:
South by the Maryland-Virginia line; and

North by a line beginning at a point at Tenth Point at the mouth of Big Annemessex River defined by Lat. 38°02.303' N, Long. 75°51.610' W; then running 334° True to a point at Porpoise Point defined by Lat. 38°03.648' N, Long. 75°52.422' W; then running along shore to a point at Hazard Point defined by Lat. 38°04.571' N, Long. 75° 52.694' W; then running 307° True to a point at South Point on Little Deal Island defined by Lat. 38°06.710' N, Long. 75°56.460' W; then running 238° True to a point at Mussel Hole Point defined by Lat. 38°04.670' N, Long. 76°00.400' W; then running 194° True to a point on the shore on the northerly tip of Smith Island defined by Lat. 38°02.367' N, Long. 76°01.050' W; and

Pocomoke Sound that are southwesterly of a straight line drawn from Maryland-Virginia boundary marker “D” defined by Lat. 37°56.473' N, Long. 75° 45.705' W; then running 342° True to a point at the most easterly point of the sound at the mouth of Gunby Creek defined by Lat. 37°58.410' N, Long. 75°46.498' W, except as provided in §C of this regulation.

Exception. Hard-shell clams may not be taken with a dredge in the waters of Apes Hole Creek westerly of a line drawn from a point at Cedar Gut defined by Lat. 37°57.448' N, Long. 75°48.752' W; then running 215° True to a point at Long Point defined by Lat. 37°56.854' N, Long. 75° 49.283 W.
An individual may not catch or attempt to catch hard-shell clams for commercial purposes on Sunday.
An individual may not possess more than 10 percent of hard-shell clams per container with a transverse dimension of less than 1 inch.
Times for Harvesting, Landing, and Delivering.
From May 1 through September 30, an individual harvesting hard-shell clams for commercial purposes:
Shall land hard-shell clams not later than 3 p.m. on the same day of harvest; and
Shall deliver hard-shell clams:
To a person who is licensed and certified to sell shellfish by the Maryland Department of Health in accordance with COMAR 10.15.04 and 10.15.07; and
Not later than 4 p.m. on the same day of harvest.
From October 1 through April 30, an individual harvesting hard-shell clams for commercial purposes:
Shall land hard-shell clams not later than 1 hour after sunset on the same day of harvest; and
Shall deliver hard-shell clams:
To a person who is licensed and certified to sell shellfish by the Maryland Department of Health in accordance with COMAR 10.15.04 and 10.15.07; and
Not later than 9 p.m. on the same day of harvest.
An individual shall notify the Natural Resources Police when there is an emergency which would prevent compliance with the times specified in this section.

In addition to the requirements of this chapter, a commercial licensee who harvests hard-shell clams shall harvest hard-shell clams in accordance with the National Shellfish Sanitation Program Model Ordinance that is incorporated by reference by the Maryland Department of Health in COMAR 10.15.07.01A.

para.text: Recreational Gear.
An individual may only use the gear specified in this regulation to catch or attempt to catch fish for recreational purposes from nontidal waters.

An individual shall comply with all seasons, creel limits, size limits, and other species-specific regulations as specified under this subtitle and Natural Resources Article, Title 4, Annotated Code of Maryland.
Traps.
An individual may not take or attempt to take fish with a trap in any trout management area described in COMAR 08.02.11.01C, D, G, and H.
An individual may not use more than one trap.
A trap shall be:
Marked with the individual’s
Name and address; or
DNRid number; and
Checked daily.
A trap shall be set:
Within 100 feet of the shore, and:
Attached by a line to the property, pier or dock; or
Marked by a buoy or pole and sign; or
By attaching the trap to a boat that is not docked.
If a trap is set on private property, the trap owner shall obtain the landowner’s permission prior to setting the trap.
If a trap is set on public property, the trap shall be set within 100 feet of the owner.
Active Line Fishing Gear.
Individuals catching or attempting to catch fish in nontidal waters may only use the following active line fishing gear:
Hook and line;
Rod and reel; and
Handline.
The gear listed in §C(1) of this regulation shall be used in a manner in which the individual is handling the gear or actively in control of the gear.
No more than two hook units per line may be used on the gear listed in §C(1) of this regulation.
Except when ice fishing, a maximum of three or a combination of three of the gear listed in §C(1) of this regulation may be used by an individual fishing in nontidal waters.
When ice fishing, a maximum of five tip ups or rods may be used.
Snagging is not legal in State waters.
Nets.
Individuals catching or attempting to catch fish in nontidal waters may only use the following nets:
Seines;
Dip nets; and
Landing nets.
Except for a landing net, a nonresident may not use nets in nontidal waters.
Except for a landing net, nets may not be used in waters described in COMAR 08.02.11.01B—H.
A person may not bait a net.
Seines in nontidal waters:
Shall have mesh no greater than 1/4 inch;
May not exceed 6 feet in width and 4 feet in height;
Shall only be used to catch minnows and other bait fish;
May not be used within 50 yards of the base of any dam or the mouth of any river or tributary; and
Shall only be emptied from shore.
Dip nets:
May be used in areas of the Potomac River, Monocacy River, and Conococheague Creek that lie within Allegany, Carroll, Frederick, and Washington counties to catch the following fish species:
Carp;
Catfish;
Northern snakehead; and
Suckers; and
May not be used in any other area or to catch any other species.
Landing nets in nontidal waters may be used to land a fish which is being caught by other means.
Projectile Gear.
Individuals catching or attempting to catch fish in nontidal waters may only use the following projectile gear:
Archery equipment;
Gig;
Spear; and
Spear gun.
Except for a gig, projectile gear shall have a retrieval line attached to it.
A gig may only be propelled by hand.
An individual may use projectile gear to take any fish except for the following species:
All trout species;
Walleye;
Striped bass;
Striped bass hybrids;
Northern pike;
Muskellunge;
Muskellunge hybrids, including tiger musky;
Largemouth and smallmouth bass;
Snapping turtles; and
Any species listed as threatened or endangered under COMAR 08.03.08.
An individual may not take or attempt to take any fish with a projectile gear in any trout management area described in COMAR 08.02.11.01B—H.
An individual may not take or attempt to take any fish with a projectile gear in State-controlled community ponds or lakes.
Additional Restrictions.
Except as provided in §E(7)(b) of this regulation, a person may not shoot projectile gear within 100 yards of any:
Human being;
Private or public swimming area;
International diving flag;
Occupied duck blind; or
Vessel other than the vessel occupied by the individual using the projectile gear.
The distance restriction in §E(7)(a) of this regulation does not apply:
To the use of gigs; or
If the person using the projectile gear receives permission from all affected parties within that area prior to engaging in fishing activities.
Hand Gear. Individuals catching or attempting to catch fish in nontidal waters may only use the following hand gear:
Hand; and
Noodling.
Recreational Gear.

Recreational gear for catching clams, crabs, and oysters is regulated elsewhere in Natural Resources Article, Title 4, Annotated Code of Maryland, and COMAR 08.02 and is excluded from this regulation.
An individual may only use the gear specified in this regulation to catch or attempt to catch fish for recreational purposes from tidal waters.

An individual using gear in accordance with this chapter shall comply with all seasons, creel limits, size limits, and other species-specific rules as specified under this subtitle and Natural Resources Article, Title 4, Annotated Code of Maryland.
Hook Requirements — Chesapeake Bay and Its Tidal Tributaries.
Chumming and Live-Lining.
When chumming, a person recreationally angling in the Chesapeake Bay or its tidal tributaries shall only use a circle hook.
Except as provided in §§B(1)(c) and (d), when live-lining, a person recreationally angling in the Chesapeake Bay or its tidal tributaries shall only use a circle hook.
When live-lining with a species of finfish listed in COMAR 08.02.20.02C, a person recreationally angling in the Chesapeake Bay or its tidal tributaries shall only use a:
Circle hook; or
“J” hook.

Except when using spot or white perch, when live-lining with a finfish that is 4 inches or less in length, a person recreationally angling in the Chesapeake Bay or its tidal tributaries shall only use a:
Circle hook; or
“J” hook.
When fishing for striped bass, a person recreationally angling in the Chesapeake Bay or its tidal tributaries shall only use a circle hook when using fish, crabs, or worms as bait, or processed bait.
During the period March 1 through May 15, a person recreationally angling in the Chesapeake Bay or its tidal tributaries:
May not use stinger hooks;
Shall only use barbless hooks while trolling; and
In addition to the requirements in §§B(1) and (2) of this regulation, when using fish, crabs, or worms as bait, or processed bait, shall only use a:
Circle hook; or
“J” hook with a gap of less than or equal to 1/2 inch between the point and the shank.

During the period May 16 through December 31, in addition to the requirements in §§B(1) and (2) of this regulation, when using fish, crabs, or worms as bait, or processed bait, a person recreationally angling in the Chesapeake Bay or its tidal tributaries shall only use a:
Circle hook; or
“J” hook.

Hook Requirements—Atlantic Ocean, Its Coastal Bays, and Their Tributaries. When fishing for striped bass, a person recreationally angling in the Atlantic Ocean, its coastal bays, or their tributaries shall only use a circle hook when using fish, crabs, or worms as bait, or processed bait.
Traps.
An individual may not use more than one trap.
A trap shall be:
Marked with the individual’s DNRid number; and
Checked daily.
A trap shall be set:
Within 100 feet of the shore, and:
Attached by a line to the property, pier or dock; or
Marked by a buoy or pole and sign; or
By attaching the trap to a boat that is not docked.
If a trap is set on private property, the trap owner shall obtain the landowner’s permission prior to setting the trap.
If a trap is set on public property, the trap shall be set within 100 feet of the owner.
Active Line Fishing Gear.
Individuals catching or attempting to catch fish in tidal waters may only use the following active line fishing gear:
Hook and line;
Rod and reel; and
Handline.
The gear listed in §E(1) of this regulation shall be used in a manner in which the individual is handling the gear or actively in control of the gear.
No more than two hook units per line may be used on the gear listed under §E(1) of this regulation.
Snagging is not legal in State waters.

During the period March 1 through May 15, no more than six lines, regardless of the number of people on board a vessel, may be used for recreationally angling from a boat when trolling in the Chesapeake Bay or its tidal tributaries.
Nonactive Line Fishing Gear.
The only nonactive line fishing gear that an individual may use to catch or attempt to catch fish in tidal waters is a jug.
An individual may use up to 10 jugs.
Jugs:
Shall have no more than 2 hooks per line and no more than one line per jug;
May only be used in tidal tributaries of the Chesapeake Bay;
May only be used from July 1 through the last day of February;
Shall be marked with the individual’s DNRid number;
Shall be attended between the hours of sunset and sunrise; and
May be used to take or attempt to take any fish except for the following species:
Largemouth and smallmouth bass;
Striped bass;
All shark species;
Snapping turtles; or
Any species listed as threatened or endangered under COMAR 08.03.08.
Nets.
Individuals catching or attempting to catch fish in tidal waters may only use the following nets:
Cast nets;
Seines;
Dip nets; and
Landing nets.
Cast nets shall have a radius not exceeding 10 feet.
Seines in tidal waters:
Shall have mesh no greater than 1/4 inch;
May not exceed 50 feet in width and 5 feet in height;
Shall only be used to catch minnows and other bait fish;
May not be emptied from a boat; and
May not be emptied on the shore or in water less than 12 inches deep.
An individual may use a landing net to land a fish which is being caught by other means.
A person may not bait a net.
Projectile Gear.
Individuals catching or attempting to catch fish in tidal waters may only use the following projectile gear:
Archery equipment;
Gig;
Spear; and
Spear gun.
Except for a gig, projectile gear shall have a retrieval line attached to it.
A gig may only be propelled by hand.
An individual may use projectile gear to take or attempt to take any fish except for the following species:
All trout species;
Walleye;
Striped bass;
Striped bass hybrids;
Northern pike;
Muskellunge;
Muskellunge hybrids, including tiger musky;
Largemouth and smallmouth bass;
Snapping turtles;
All shark species;
American lobster; and
Any species listed as threatened or endangered under COMAR 08.03.08.
Additional Restrictions.
Except as provided in §F(5)(b) of this regulation, a person may not shoot projectile gear within 100 yards of any:
Human being;
Private or public swimming area;
International diving flag;
Occupied duck blind; or
Vessel other than the vessel occupied by the individual using the projectile gear.
The distance restriction in §F(5)(a) of this regulation does not apply:
To the use of gigs; or
If the person using the projectile gear receives permission from all affected parties within that area prior to engaging in fishing activities.
Hand Gear. Individuals catching or attempting to catch fish in tidal waters may only use the following hand gear:
Hand; and
Noodling.

para.text: A person licensed to buy, process, pack, resell, market, or otherwise deal in soft-shell clams, hard-shell clams, or oysters in accordance with Natural Resources Article, §4-701, Annotated Code of Maryland, shall:
Accept soft-shell clams, hard-shell clams, or oysters only:
From a licensed harvester;
On the same day of harvest; and
If tagged as required in accordance with COMAR 08.02.02.04, 08.02.04.04, or 08.02.07.04.
Follow the requirements of the National Shellfish Sanitation Program Model Ordinance that is incorporated by reference in COMAR 10.15.07.01A; and
Implement Vibrio parahaemolyticus control measures in accordance with COMAR 10.15.07.06.
A person who is licensed and certified to sell shellfish by the Maryland Department of Health in accordance with COMAR 10.15.04 and 10.15.07 shall:
Follow the requirements of the National Shellfish Sanitation Program Model Ordinance that is incorporated by reference in COMAR 10.15.07.01A; and
Implement Vibrio parahaemolyticus control measures in accordance with COMAR 10.15.07.06.
Any person possessing a license to deal in soft-shell clams shall maintain and submit to the Department any records the Department may require.
Declaration.

Prior to purchasing soft-shell clams of the species Mya arenaria, hard-shell clams, or oysters, a person licensed in accordance with Natural Resources Article, §4-701, Annotated Code of Maryland and licensed and certified to sell shellfish by the Maryland Department of Health in accordance with COMAR 10.15.04 and 10.15.07, shall on a form provided by the Department:
Declare their intent to deal in shellfish; and
Provide their certification number issued by the Maryland Department of Health.

Prior to selling their own catch of soft-shell clams of the species Mya arenaria, hard-shell clams, or oysters, a harvester licensed in accordance with Natural Resources Article, §4-701, Annotated Code of Maryland and licensed and certified to sell shellfish by the Maryland Department of Health in accordance with COMAR 10.15.04 and 10.15.07, shall on a form provided by the Department:
Declare their intent to deal in shellfish; and
Provide their certification number issued by the Maryland Department of Health.
A declaration of intent under this section shall be valid for the remainder of the license year.

para.text: In this chapter, the following terms have the meanings indicated.
Terms Defined.
“Board” means the State Board of Dental Examiners.
“Central Repository” means the Criminal Justice Information System Central Repository of the Department of Public Safety and Correctional Services.
“Dental assistant” means an individual, other than an individual licensed in the State as a dentist or a dental hygienist, who directly assists a dentist in the practice of dentistry.

“Dental Assisting National Board (DANB)” means the national certification and credentialing agency for dental assistants that examines and certifies qualified individuals as orthodontic EFDAs and general duties EFDAs.
“Direct supervision” means that the supervising dentist is in the dental office personally:
Diagnoses the condition to be treated;
Authorizes the procedure; and
Evaluates the performance of the dental assistant, before the dismissal of the patient.
“General duties EFDA” means an individual who is certified by the Board to perform the intraoral procedures of a general duties expanded function dental assistant as set forth in this chapter.

“General supervision” means the supervision of a dental assistant by a dentist where the dentist may or may not be present in the dental office when the dental assistant performs the dental assisting procedures.
“Level one dental assistant” means a dental assistant who may perform the duties of a level one dental assistant as provided in this chapter without being certified by the Board.
“Orthodontic EFDA” means an individual who is certified by the Board to perform the intraoral procedures of an orthodontic expanded function dental assistant as set forth in this chapter.

section.heading: Classifications No Longer Recognized by the Board.

para.text: Dental Assistant Recognized as Qualified in Orthodontics.
The Board no longer recognizes the classification “dental assistant recognized as qualified in orthodontics.”

A dental assistant previously recognized by the Board as a “dental assistant recognized as qualified in orthodontics” shall obtain certification from the Board as an orthodontic EFDA before the dental assistant may perform any of the duties of an orthodontic EFDA as set forth in Regulation .24 of this chapter.
Dental Assistant Recognized as Qualified in General Duties.
The Board no longer recognizes the classification “dental assistant recognized as qualified in general duties.”

A dental assistant previously recognized by the Board as a “dental assistant recognized as qualified in general duties” may, under the direct supervision of a licensed dentist, perform the duties of a level one dental assistant as set forth in Regulation .03 of this chapter without obtaining certification from the Board.
A Level one dental assistant shall be at least 18 years old.

Except as otherwise provided, a dentist may use the services of a level one dental assistant to perform the following intraoral procedures under the direct supervision of a licensed dentist without first receiving certification from the Board:
Rinsing and aspiration of the oral cavity;
Retraction of the lips, cheeks, tongue, and flaps;
Placement and removal of the materials for the isolation of the dentition, provided that the material is not retained by the dentition;
Instructing on oral hygiene;
Taking alginate or digital impressions for study models or diagnostic casts;
Constructing athletic mouthguards on models;
Applying topical anesthetic;
Light curing;
Checking for loose bands;

Assisting in performing intraoral photography, other than conventional or digital X-ray, under the general supervision of a licensed dentist who reviews the photography and authorizes the treatment plan;
Placing and removing cotton rolls;
Delivery of restorative material with dentist at chairside;
Fluoride application — rinse or foam tray or fluoride varnish;
Taking and recording vital signs, including blood pressure and pulse readings;
Performing vitality tests;
Taking alginate impressions for intraoral appliances;
Taking digital and electronic impressions;
Applying desensitizing agents;
Placing or removing a rubber dam;
Fabricating indirect restorations in a dental office;
Placing or removing a matrix band;
Drying a root canal;
Preparing and fitting stainless steel crowns;
Placing or removing a retraction cord;
Fabricating temporary crowns;
Cementing temporary crowns or restorations;
Removing temporary crowns;
Removing excess cement;
Removing or replacing a periodontal dressing (except placing the original periodontal dressing);
Removing sutures;
Bite registration;
Placing temporary restorations;
Placing and removing wedges; and
Fabricating on models:
Athletic mouthguards;
Bleaching trays;
Fluoride trays;
Impression trays; and
Nightguards.
A level one dental assistant may perform duties in accordance with §B of this regulation if a licensed dentist:
Provides the level one dental assistant with specific instructions to perform the intraoral procedure; and
Except as otherwise provided, directly supervises the level one dental assistant performing the intraoral procedure.
A dentist who supervises a level one dental assistant shall ensure that the level one dental assistant is properly trained in:
Infection control; and
Cardiopulmonary resuscitation.

section.heading: Dental Assisting National Board.
section.text: The Board shall in consultation with DANB determine:

para.text: The subjects, scope, form, and passing score for EFDA examinations; and
The grading method.

section.heading: Qualifications for General Duties Expanded Function Dental Assistants.

para.text: To qualify for a Board certification to be a general duties EFDA, an applicant shall:
Be of good moral character;
Be at least 18 years old;
Be a high school graduate or have attained a high school equivalency;
Submit to a State criminal history records check;

Have successfully completed a Board-approved course of at least 60 hours related to Maryland general duties EFDA which shall include at least 15 hours of in-person hands-on clinical training apart from the in-person hands-on clinical training required by Regulation .18A(2) of this chapter.
Have the appropriate general duties EFDA certification from the Dental Assisting National Board;
Submit proof of having passed the Maryland Jurisprudence Examination on Dental Assisting with a score of 75 or greater in each required section; and
Maintain cardiopulmonary resuscitation certification from one of the following programs:
The American Heart Association’s Basic Life Support for Healthcare Providers;
The American Red Cross’s Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation for Professional Rescuers; or
An equivalent program approved by the Board.
Criminal History Records Check.
An applicant shall apply to the Central Repository for a State criminal history records check.
An applicant shall submit to the Central Repository:
Two complete sets of legible fingerprints taken on forms approved by the Director of the Central Repository and the Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation; and
The fee authorized under Criminal Procedure Article, §10-221(b)(7), Annotated Code of Maryland, for access to State criminal history records.

In accordance with Criminal Procedure Article, §§10–201—10–229, Annotated Code of Maryland, the Central Repository shall forward to the Board and to the applicant the criminal history record information of the applicant.

If criminal history record information is reported to the Central Repository after the date of the initial criminal history records check, the Central Repository shall provide to the Board and the individual a revised printed statement of the individual’s State criminal history record.
Information obtained from the Central Repository under this section:
Is confidential;
May not be redisseminated; and
May be used only for the licensing purpose authorized by this chapter.
The applicant may contest the contents of the printed statement issued by the Central Repository in accordance with Criminal Procedure Article, §10–223, Annotated Code of Maryland.

Subject to the notice and hearing provisions set forth in Health Occupations Article, §4-318, Annotated Code of Maryland, the Board may deny certification under this chapter if the applicant has been convicted of or has plead guilty or nolo contendere to a felony or to a crime involving moral turpitude, whether or not any appeal or other proceeding is pending to have the conviction or plea set aside.

section.heading: Application for Board Certification—General Duties Expanded Function Dental Assistants.

para.text: To apply for a Board certification as a general duties EFDA, an applicant shall:
Submit to the Board an application on the form provided by the Board;
Submit a recent photograph of the applicant not to exceed 3 inches by 3 inches accompanied by a notarized statement attesting to the photograph’s authenticity;
Pay the application fee set by the Board in COMAR 10.44.20;
Provide evidence satisfactory to the Board that the applicant meets the qualifications for Board certification as a general duties EFDA as set forth in Regulation .05A of this chapter; and
Provide any other pertinent documents or information requested by the Board.

The applicant shall include with the application proof of completion of a 60-hour Board-approved course of instruction in general duties EFDA in the form of a letter from one of the institutions referenced in Regulation .18C of this chapter indicating that the applicant has successfully completed the course.
The letter referenced in §B of this regulation shall:
Be on the letterhead of one of the institutions referenced in Regulation .18C of this chapter;
Contain a raised embossed school seal or institution seal; and
Contain the original signature of either:
The dean or principal of the school or program; or
The head of the department.
The Board may issue a Board certification as a general duties EFDA after the Board’s review of:
The applicant’s application;
The applicant’s qualifications;
The applicant’s criminal history records check; and
Any other pertinent documents or information that may affect the applicant’s ability to safely provide dental assistant duties.

section.heading: Qualifications for Orthodontic Expanded Function Dental Assistants.

para.text: To qualify for a Board certification to be an orthodontic EFDA, an applicant shall:
Be of good moral character;
Be at least 18 years old;
Be a high school graduate or have attained a high school equivalency;
Submit to a State criminal history records check in accordance with §B of this regulation;
Have successfully completed a Board-approved course of at least 35 hours related to Maryland orthodontic EFDA, of which at least 10 hours shall include in-person hands-on clinical training;
Have the appropriate orthodontic EFDA certification from the Dental Assisting National Board;
Submit proof of having passed the Maryland Jurisprudence Examination on Dental Assisting with a score of at least 75 or greater in each required section;
Maintain cardiopulmonary resuscitation certification from one of the following programs:
The American Heart Association’s Basic Life Support for Healthcare Providers;
The American Red Cross’s Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation for Professional Rescuers; or
An equivalent program approved by the Board.
Criminal History Records Check.
An applicant shall apply to the Central Repository for a State criminal history records check.
An applicant shall submit to the Central Repository:
Two complete sets of legible fingerprints taken on forms approved by the Director of the Central Repository and the Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation; and
The fee authorized under Criminal Procedure Article, §10-221(b)(7), Annotated Code of Maryland, for access to State criminal history records.

In accordance with Criminal Procedure Article, §§10–201—10–229, Annotated Code of Maryland, the Central Repository shall forward to the Board and to the applicant the criminal history record information of the applicant..

If criminal history record information is reported to the Central Repository after the date of the initial criminal history records check, the Central Repository shall provide to the Board and the individual a revised printed statement of the individual’s State criminal history record.
Information obtained from the Central Repository under this section:
Is confidential;
May not be redisseminated; and
May be used only for the licensing purpose authorized by this chapter.
The applicant may contest the contents of the printed statement issued by the Central Repository in accordance with Criminal Procedure Article, §10–223, Annotated Code of Maryland.

Subject to the notice and hearing provisions set forth in Health Occupations Article, §4-318, Annotated Code of Maryland, the Board may deny certification under this chapter if the applicant has been convicted of or has plead guilty or nolo contendere to a felony or to a crime involving moral turpitude, whether or not any appeal or other proceeding is pending to have the conviction or plea set aside.

section.heading: Application for Board Certification for Orthodontic Expanded Function Dental Assistants.

para.text: To apply for a Board certification as an orthodontic EFDA, an applicant shall:
Submit to the Board an application on the form provided by the Board;
Submit a recent photograph of the applicant not to exceed 3 inches by 3 inches accompanied by a notarized statement attesting to the photograph’s authenticity;
Pay the application fee set by the Board in COMAR 10.44.20;
Provide evidence satisfactory to the Board that the applicant meets the qualifications for Board certification as an orthodontic EFDA as set forth in Regulation .07A of this chapter; and
Provide any other pertinent documents or information requested by the Board.

The applicant shall include with the application proof of completion of a 35-hour Board-approved course of instruction in orthodontic EFDA in the form of a letter from one of the institutions referenced in Regulation .18E of this chapter indicating that the applicant has successfully completed the course.
The letter referenced in §B of this regulation shall:
Be on the letterhead of one of the institutions referenced in Regulation .18E of this chapter;
Contain a raised embossed school seal or institution seal; and
Contain the original signature of either:
The dean or principal of the school or program; or
The head of the department.
The Board may issue a Board certification as an orthodontic EFDA after the Board’s review of:
The applicant’s application;
The applicant’s qualifications;
The applicant’s criminal history records check; and
Any other pertinent documents or information that may affect the applicant’s ability to safely provide dental assistant duties.

section.heading: Dental Assistants Previously Recognized as Qualified in Orthodontics.

para.text: Except as otherwise provided in this regulation, in order to perform the intraoral procedures of an orthodontic EFDA, a dental assistant recognized by the Board as qualified in orthodontics prior to August 31, 2026 shall:
Apply to the Board for certification as an orthodontic EFDA;
Submit a recent photograph of the applicant not to exceed 3 inches by 3 inches accompanied by a notarized statement attesting to the photograph’s authenticity;
Pay the appropriate fee; and
Meet all of the qualifications of an orthodontic EFDA set forth in Regulation .07 of this chapter.
A dental assistant recognized by the Board as qualified in orthodontics prior to August 31, 2026 is not required to take the Board-approved course or take the DANB orthodontic EFDA examination.

After initial orthodontic EFDA certification, a dental assistant recognized by the Board as qualified in orthodontics prior to August 31, 2026 who becomes an orthodontic EFDA shall meet all of the requirements of renewal in accordance with Regulation .11 of this chapter.
Grace Period.
A dental assistant recognized by the Board as qualified in orthodontics prior to August 31, 2026 may lawfully perform the duties of an orthodontic EFDA until February 28, 2027.

A dental assistant recognized by the Board as qualified in orthodontics prior to August 31, 2026 who has not become an orthodontic EFDA February 28, 2027 may not perform the duties of either a dental assistant recognized as qualified in orthodontics or an orthodontic EFDA.

section.heading: Board Issuance of Expanded Function Dental Assistant Certificates.

para.text: The Board shall issue an appropriate certificate to an applicant who meets the requirements of Health Occupations Article, Title 4, Subtitle 3, Annotated Code of Maryland, this chapter, and any other applicable laws or regulations.
The Board shall include on each certificate that the Board issues:
The designation of the certificate as either orthodontic expanded function or general duties expanded function dental assistant;
The name of the certified individual;
The date the certificate was issued;
A serial number or certificate number;
The signatures of the President and Secretary of the Board which may be electronic; and
The seal of the Board.

section.heading: Term and Renewal of Expanded Function Dental Assistant Certificates.

para.text: Term of Certificate. A certification as an orthodontic EFDA or a general duties EFDA shall expire on October 31 of the second year following the effective date of the certificate unless it is renewed for an additional 2-year term in accordance with this regulation.
Renewal Notice. At least 1 month before a certificate expires, the Board shall send to the EFDA, by electronic means to the last known electronic address of the EFDA, a renewal notice that states:
The date on which the current certificate expires;
The date by which the application shall be received by the Board for the renewal to be issued and forwarded before expiration; and
The amount of the renewal fee set by the Board in accordance with COMAR 10.44.20.
Renewal of Certificate. Before a certification as an orthodontic EFDA or a general duties EFDA expires, the individual may renew the certification for an additional 2 years if the individual:
Applies for renewal of the certification on the form provided by the Board;
Pays to the Board a renewal fee set by the Board in accordance with COMAR 10.44.20; and
Successfully completes the required continuing education requirements set forth in Regulation .16 of this chapter.

section.heading: Renewal and Reinstatement of Expired Certificates.

para.text: Renewal of Expired Certificates Held for 30 Days or Less.
After the expiration date of a certificate to practice EFDA in the State, the certificate holder may renew the certificate within 30 days of its expiration if the certificate holder:
Is otherwise entitled to be issued a certificate;
Submits to the Board a completed renewal application on the form provided by the Board; and
Pays the Board the renewal fee and late fee in accordance with COMAR 10.44.20.

An individual who uses continuing education credits to renew their certificate after the expiration date of their certificate may not use the same continuing education credits for the renewal period succeeding the renewal period in which the continuing education credits were used.
Reinstatement of Expired Certificates.
An individual holding an expired orthodontic EFDA certificate or an individual holding an expired general duties EFDA certificate may apply for reinstatement if the individual:
Has held an expired orthodontic EFDA certificate or an expired general duties EFDA certificate for more than 30 days and less than 3 years;
Is otherwise entitled to be reinstated;
Completes the reinstatement application on the form provided by the Board;

Provides proof of completion of 15 hours of dental assisting continuing education from Board-approved courses of which 3 hours shall be in infection control as provided in Regulation .16 of this chapter; and
Pays to the Board a certification reinstatement fee set in COMAR 10.44.20.

An individual who uses continuing education credits to renew their certificate after the expiration date of their certificate may not use the same continuing education credits for the renewal period succeeding the renewal period in which the continuing education credits were used.
Certificates Expired for 3 or More Years.
An individual holding an expired orthodontic EFDA certificate or an expired general duties EFDA certificate which has been expired for 3 years or more may not apply for reinstatement.

An individual holding an expired orthodontic EFDA certificate or an expired general duties EFDA certificate which has been expired for 3 years or more shall meet the qualifications for initial certification set forth in either Regulation .07 of this chapter for orthodontic EFDAs, or Regulation .05 of this chapter for general duties EFDAs.

section.heading: Lost or Destroyed Certificates.
section.text: The Board shall issue a certificate to replace a lost or destroyed certificate if the EFDA pays the fee set by the Board in accordance with COMAR 10.44.20 that approximates the actual cost of replacing the certificate.

para.text: Regulations. The supervising dentist in charge of a dental office where an orthodontic EFDA or a general duties EFDA performs intraoral procedures shall display a copy of this chapter in a conspicuous place in the office for the information of office personnel.

Certificates. The supervising dentist in charge of a dental office where one or more orthodontic EFDAs or one or more general duties EFDAs perform intraoral duties shall display the certificates and any current renewal certificates conspicuously in the office where the holders are engaged in practice.

section.heading: Retention of Certification and Qualification Documents.

para.text: An individual certified as either an orthodontic EFDA or a general duties EFDA shall keep their original Board certification and their original current renewal document in the office where the dental assistant is employed for the greatest number of hours.

An individual certified as either an orthodontic EFDA or a general duties EFDA who works in more than one dental office shall keep a copy of their original Board certification and a copy of their current renewal document in all other offices in which the dental assistant is employed.
In addition to the requirements set forth in Regulation .11 of this chapter, an orthodontic EFDA or a general duties EFDA seeking certification renewal shall, at minimum, complete:
15 hours of Board-approved continuing education specifically designed to enhance their clinical knowledge and ability to perform their duties; and
A 3-hour Board-approved course on infection control which shall count toward the required 15 hours of continuing education.
A clock hour constitutes 1 hour of continuing education.
Certificate holders shall have a 2-year period to complete the required continuing education in the 2-year period preceding the expiration date of the immediately preceding certificate.

A Board-approved continuing education sponsor shall, at a minimum, issue a hard copy of a Continuing Education Certificate of Completion to an EFDA who successfully completes a Board-approved continuing education course.
The Certificate of Completion set forth in §A of this regulation shall contain at least the following:
The exact name of the course sponsor as approved by the Board;
The full business address of the course sponsor;
The exact name of the course as approved by the Board;
An indication whether the course was taught in person or electronically;
The full name of the student recipient;
The number of credit hours obtained;
The name of the course instructors;
The signature of the course instructors which may be electronic; and
The Board’s course approval number.
General Duties EFDA. The course identified in Regulation .05A(5) of this chapter shall include at a minimum, the following:
6 hours of instruction on nitrous oxide monitoring;
2 hours of in-person hands-on clinical training, including the direct observation of the performance of procedures; and
4 hours of didactic training, including at least the following subjects:
The history, philosophy, and psychology of nitrous oxide minimal sedation;
The definition and descriptions of the physiological and psychological aspects of pain and anxiety;
Concepts and management of pain and anxiety;
Indications and contraindications for nitrous oxide sedation;
Anatomy and physiology of pediatric and adult respiration;
Medical assessment of a patient before nitrous oxide administration by a dentist or a dental hygienist;
Moderate sedation, deep sedation, and general anesthesia versus nitrous oxide;
Pharmacological and physiological effects of nitrous oxide, including drug interactions;

A description of the stages of drug induced central nervous system depression through all levels of consciousness and unconsciousness with emphasis on the distinction between the conscious and unconscious state;
Monitoring of a patient to whom nitrous oxide has been administered, including the monitoring of a patient’s vital functions;
Recognition and management of complications and medical emergencies;
Occupational exposure; and
Preventing, recognizing, and managing possible complications of inhalation sedation.

The course identified in Regulation .05A(5) shall adequately prepare the student to competently and safely perform each of the intraoral procedures that a general duties EFDA may perform under Regulation .22 of this chapter.
The course identified in Regulation .05A(5) of this chapter shall be part of:
A U.S. Department of Labor Jobs Corps dental assisting program;
A dental assisting program located within an institution of postsecondary education that is accredited by an accrediting institution recognized by the U.S. Department of Education;

A dental assisting program that is located within a high school and is recognized by an accrediting body recognized by the U.S. Department of Education or the high school accrediting body of a state, or
A dental assisting program that is accredited by the Council on Dental Accreditation, or a successor organization.

Orthodontic EFDA. The course identified in Regulation .07A(5) of this chapter shall adequately prepare the student to competently and safely perform each of the orthodontic procedures that an orthodontic EFDA may perform under Regulation .24 of this chapter.
The course identified in Regulation .07A(5) of this chapter shall be part of:
A U.S. Department of Labor Job Corps dental assisting program;
A dental Assisting Program located within an institution of postsecondary education that is accredited by an accrediting institution recognized by the U.S. Department of Education;

A dental assisting program that is located within a high school and is recognized by an accrediting body recognized by the U.S. Department of Education or the high school accrediting body of a state; or
A dental assisting program that is accredited by the Council on Dental Accreditation, or a successor organization.

section.heading: Requirements for Instructors of Expanded Function Dental Assistant and Courses.

para.text: Any instructor of either an orthodontic EFDA course or a general duties EFDA course shall:
Be qualified by education and experience to provide instruction in the subject matter; and
Provide instruction in a competent manner.
Encumbered License.
To the extent that an instructor is a licensed dentist or a licensed dental hygienist, the instructor may not have an encumbered license in any state.
For the purposes of the regulation, an encumbered license does not include a reprimand issued more than 5 years prior to the date of instructing a Board-approved course.

At least once every calendar year, each Board-approved orthodontic EFDA course and each Board-approved general duties EFDA course shall be assessed by a dentist licensed in the State other than the dentist who is the instructor.

The results of the assessment shall be entered on the form provided by the Board and maintained in accordance with §D of this regulation by the dentist performing the assessment and the entity presenting the course.
Course Deficiencies. If an assessment indicates that there are course deficiencies, the entity presenting the course shall:
Immediately correct the deficiencies;
Provide the Board in writing within 5 business days:
Notice of the deficiencies;
A copy of the assessment; and
Any corrective measures taken.

All assessments shall be maintained by the dentist conducting the assessment and the entity presenting the course for at least 5 years and be made available to the Board upon written request within 5 working days of the request.
The Board may rescind approval of a previously approved orthodontic EFDA course or a general duties EFDA course if the Board determines that the course:
Does not meet the requirements of this chapter;
Does not meet its stated objectives; or
The sponsor has committed fraud or made other misrepresentations to the Board.
On its own initiative or on a written complaint filed with the Board by any person, the Board may conduct an investigation of the:
Sponsor of the course;
Course site; or
Instructors of the course.

section.heading: Procedures Permitted to be Performed by General Duties EFDAs.

para.text: Except for an individual licensed as a dentist or a dental hygienist under Health Occupations Article, Title 4, Annotated Code of Maryland, an individual shall be expressly certified by the State Board of Dental Examiners as a general duties EFDA before the individual may perform any of the following intraoral procedures:
Placing dental sealants;
Coronal polishing only to remove stain or biofilm, in connection with a dental prophylaxis:

As determined necessary and appropriate, secondary to the more complex dental procedures of a dental prophylaxis, such as removal of hard and soft deposits and stain of the tooth crown, root surfaces, and periodontal pockets; and
If applicable, in consultation with the treating dental hygienist or before a dentist performs an esthetic or cementation procedure;
Applying silver diamine fluoride;
Monitoring nitrous oxide by observing a patient;
During the flow of nitrous oxide;
During the reduction of the flow of nitrous oxide;
During the shutting off of equipment controlling the flow of nitrous oxide; and
At all times in between the start of the flow of nitrous oxide until the nitrous oxide has been terminated and the patient has fully awoken and is coherent;
Acid etching; and
Applying bonding agents.

In addition to the intraoral procedures set forth in §A of this regulation, a general duties EFDA may perform the intraoral procedures of level one dental assistant set forth in Regulation .03B of this chapter if performed in accordance with the requirements of Regulation .03C of this chapter.

section.heading: Monitoring Nitrous Oxide—Standards of Practice for General Duties EFDAs.

para.text: A general duties EFDA who monitors a patient to whom nitrous oxide has been administered may not:
Increase the nitrous oxide levels;
Monitor more than one patient at a time;
Treat any other patient during the course of the monitoring; or
Leave the operatory during the monitoring except in emergency circumstances.
A dentist who orders a general duties EFDA to monitor a patient to whom nitrous oxide has been administered shall:
Have a written emergency plan;
Remain in the dental office and in close proximity to be summoned in the event of an emergency; and
Discharge the patient.

section.heading: Procedures Permitted to be Performed by Orthodontic EFDAs.

para.text: Except for an individual licensed as a dentist or a dental hygienist under Health Occupations Article, Title 4, Annotated Code of Maryland, an individual shall be expressly certified by the State Board of Dental Examiners as an orthodontic EFDA before the individual may perform any of the following intraoral procedures:
Preparing and fitting orthodontic bands;
Placing and removing arch wires;
Cementing of orthodontic bands, placement of bonded attachments, or removal of cemented or bonded orthodontic bands and attachments;
Placing elastics and ligatures;
Selecting headgear;
Acid etching; and
Applying bonding agents.

In addition to the intraoral procedures set forth in §A of this regulation, an orthodontic EFDA may perform the intraoral procedures of a level one dental assistant set forth in Regulation .03B of this chapter if performed in accordance with the requirements of Regulation .03C of this chapter.

section.heading: Radiographs.
section.text: A dentist may not permit a dental assistant to place and expose radiographs unless the individual is certified to practice dental radiation technology in accordance with COMAR 10.44.19.

section.heading: Simultaneous Certification.
section.text: An individual may be simultaneously certified as an orthodontic EFDA, a general duties EFDA, a dental radiation technologist, or any combination thereof.

section.heading: Dental Sealant Program Exception — General Supervision.

para.text: This regulation applies only to the dental assistant dental sealant program described in §C of this regulation.

Notwithstanding any other provision of this chapter, a level one dental assistant may provide the following dental assisting duties under the general supervision of a dentist for a dental sealant program:
Instructing on oral hygiene;
Cleaning and disinfecting environmental surfaces and equipment;
Preparing materials for the application of sealants;
Retracting lips, cheek, and tongue;
Placing and removing materials for the isolation of the dentition, if the material is not retained by the dentition;
Transferring instruments and sealants to a dentist or dental hygienist;
Rinsing and aspirating of the oral cavity; and
Sterilizing instruments.
Under the general supervision of a dentist, a level one dental assistant may only perform the duties enumerated in §B of this regulation:
For a facility that has been granted a waiver of on-site supervision for a dental hygienist under COMAR 10.44.21; and
While assisting a dental hygienist who has received a waiver of on-site supervision under COMAR 10.44.21.
A dental assistant performing dental assistant duties under this regulation may not place dental sealants.
A level one dental assistant who provides dental assistant duties under this regulation shall maintain cardiopulmonary resuscitation certification from one of the following programs:
The American Heart Association's Basic Life Support for Healthcare Providers;
The American Red Cross's Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation for Professional Rescuers; or
An equivalent program approved by the Board.
A level one dental assistant who provides dental assistant duties under this regulation shall have at least 400 hours of dental assisting clinical practice in direct patient care.
An orthodontic EFDA who provides dental assistant duties under this regulation shall successfully complete a Board-approved course of at least 3 hours in infection control every renewal cycle.

A level one dental assistant who provides dental assistant duties under this regulation shall successfully complete a Board-approved course with at least 3 hours in infection control before providing dental assistant duties under this regulation, and within every 2 calendar years thereafter.

A facility that uses a level one dental assistant to provide dental assistant duties under this regulation shall ensure that there is a written agreement between the supervising dentist and the dental assistant practicing under general supervision that clearly sets forth the terms and conditions under which the dental assistant may practice, including a statement that the dental assistant may provide dental assistant duties without the supervising dentist on the premises.
Each facility that uses the services of a level one dental assistant to provide dental assistant duties under this regulation shall maintain for 5 years for inspection by the Board:
The name of the dentist providing general supervision to the dental assistant;
The name and current address of the dental assistant;
The name and address of each institution where the dental assistant provided dental assistant duties; and
Any dates in which the dental assistant provided dental assistant duties.
This regulation does not affect the duties a level one dental assistant may lawfully perform under the direct supervision of a dentist under this chapter.
A violation of this regulation may result in:
Revocation of the facility's right to operate under a waiver of on-site supervision for dental hygienists; or
Revocation of the facility's right to utilize the services of a dental assistant under this regulation.
Penalties.
For violations of this regulation, a dentist and a dental hygienist is subject to the penalties set forth in Regulation .29 of this chapter.
A dentist or a dental hygienist who uses the services of a dental assistant who is not qualified or for purposes other than what are permitted under this regulation may be found guilty of:
Unprofessional conduct in accordance with Health Occupations Article, §4-315, Annotated Code of Maryland; or
Violating any rule or regulation adopted by the Board in accordance with Health Occupations Article, §4-315, Annotated Code of Maryland.

section.heading: Expanded Function Dental Assistant Practicing After Certificate Has Expired.
section.text: A supervising dentist who allows an EFDA to practice EFDA duties after their certificate has expired may be found guilty of unprofessional conduct under Health Occupations Article, §4-315(a)(16), Annotated Code of Maryland.

section.heading: Violations.
section.text: A dentist who uses the services of a dental assistant who is not qualified or for purposes other than what is permitted may be found guilty of:

para.text: Unprofessional conduct in accordance with Health Occupations Article, §4-315(a)(16), Annotated Code of Maryland;
Violating any rule or regulation adopted by the Board in accordance with Health Occupations Article, §4-315(a)(20), Annotated Code of Maryland;
Allowing a dental assistant to assist in the practice of dentistry in violation of Health Occupations Article, §4-315(a)(38), Annotated Code of Maryland;
Violating COMAR 10.44.23; or
Violating any other applicable law or regulation.

section.heading: Severability.
section.text: If any provision of this chapter or its application to any person or circumstance is held invalid, the invalidity does not affect other provisions or applications of this chapter which can be given effect without the invalid provision or application, and to this end the provisions of this chapter are severable.
